claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite containing either discrete W particles or an interconnected W ligament network in a Cu matrix.
The untreated W–Cu interface is prone to interphase diffusion, phase separation, and void formation.
A thin refractory high-entropy-alloy interlayer, such as (CrFeTiTa)70W30, can be introduced at W–Cu interfaces.
The high-entropy interlayer should be uniform across the W–Cu interfaces.
The high-entropy interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier that reduces W–Cu intermixing.
The high-entropy interlayer accommodates thermal-expansion mismatch between W and Cu.
Reduced interdiffusion and interfacial stress suppress phase separation and void formation.
Suppressing interfacial degradation preserves continuous W/Cu contact and a continuous heat-transfer path.
Preserving the continuous heat-transfer path increases overall thermal conductivity.
Compared with an untreated W–Cu composite, the interlayer-treated composite will have fewer interfacial voids under equivalent high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Compared with an untreated W–Cu composite, the interlayer-treated composite will have a more stable phase distribution.
Compared with an untreated W–Cu composite, the interlayer-treated composite will have higher thermal conductivity under equivalent high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components are relevant to high-thermal-flux fusion service.
Refractory (CrFeTiTa)70W30 and VFeTiTaW high-entropy alloys have been prepared and evaluated for thermal and irradiation resistance as candidate interlayers for W/CuCrZr joints.
Processing temperatures should remain below the level at which undesirable phase growth compromises the selected high-entropy alloy.
The intervention's effectiveness may diminish at temperatures substantially above the high-entropy alloy's stability limit.
The intervention's effectiveness may diminish at irradiation doses substantially above those used in prior experimental tests.
The optimum interlayer thickness and uniformity, and its behavior during very long simultaneous thermal and irradiation exposure, are uncertain.
